scope: Native external GUI create, Debian login-prompt/input echo, destroy and recreation in one Intel seL4 boot
transport: Native Tauri on Spark, Xvfb :89; binary CC Unix socket forwarded via puck to Intel madmax using SSH stream-local forwarding

first_guest.result: Debian GNU/Linux 13 login prompt rendered; exact typed marker echoed through guest console; Destroy returned empty inventory

second_guest.result: Fresh Linux boot and Debian GNU/Linux 13 login prompt rendered; exact second marker echoed; Destroy returned empty inventory

observed_rough_edges: Autoconnect before target readiness returned failed to fill whole buffer; Connect succeeded after root boot completion.

Replacing RAM 512 by typing 1024 produced 128024 due to per-keystroke clamping. The first Start returned create_guest err 8 and inventory remained empty. No causal attribution to RAM versus readiness is established.
Native number spinner set RAM to 1024 before successful creation; RAM edit bug is tracked as task_c0e001b8901a4a2fad3ffd2fd15722e7.
limitations: Input markers are echoed at the guest login prompt; interactive authenticated shell login is not claimed by this GUI run.
The 1024 MiB launch field records the request, not proof of dynamically allocated or guest-visible RAM.
Graphical guest framebuffer, concurrent guest streams, abrupt-disconnect/input-release behavior and resource/storage acceptance are outside this run.
The separate intermittent serial qualification failure and required GitHub checks remain unresolved; canonical integration and release are pending.
result: Passed both native GUI lifecycle cycles in one seL4 boot
cleanup: Destroyed both guests through the GUI before stopping the owned app, QEMU, SSH forwards and Xvfb. GUI Make exited 2 after intentional SIGTERM; target Make exited 0 after intentional QEMU SIGTERM. These launcher exits are cleanup outcomes, not automated test verdicts.
